sweep_summary: The only works with stress in the title for tagb1258 (Warner 1979, 'Walking on two feet') is a UH Manoa anthropology dissertation (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as an ethnographic work) and is irrelevant to stress.org was blocked, so this search of works with stress in the title fell back to open repositories (sealang, zorc.net, Glottolog, archive.org, Wikipedia) plus files already downloaded in this reading. The best first-hand statement read is Zorc 1977:218 (own Aborlan data, n. 8 p. 287): Palawano, Aborlan and Agutaynen 'do not have contrastive word accent', backed by Zorc's review of Thiessen 1981 (accent differences in Aborlan idiolectal, from Tagalog/Bisayan superstrata; Thiessen 1981:10 says no Palawan variety distinguishes words by accent alone, accent on one of the last two syllables in the southern varieties). Green 1979 (PL A-50, newly downloaded), Hussey 1966, Reid 1971 entry 41 and Zorc 2023 are silent. Language is not in the catalog; suggested coding: no contrastive word stress (position unspecified). Acquisition priorities: Thiessen 1980/1981 (medium; OCLC 702398688) and Hussey 1965 (medium).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Aborlan Tagbanwa has no contrastive (phonemic) word accent: unlike Bisayan and Tagalog, words are not distinguished by stress placement. The source does not state where non-contrastive prominence falls. Second-hand (Thiessen 1981:10 as quoted in Zorc's review, held by the project): in the Palawan languages accent falls on one of the last two syllables of the word and is never contrastive; Zorc's review adds that in his own Aborlan data accent differences are idiolectal and induced by Tagalog/Bisayan superstrata.
new_statements.exceptions: Zorc's review of Thiessen (p. 109): apparent accent contrasts in Aborlan, Brooke's Point Palawano and Batak 'are the result of mimicry of Tagalog or Bisayan forms known to and by individual speakers' and 'often differ from one idiolect to another'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('contrastive word accent'); a one-sentence remark in a comparative study of Bisayan, based on the author's own Aborlan field data cross-checked against Reid 1971; no citation forms or examples given for Aborlan. Thiessen's 'last two syllables' rule (second-hand) is stated for suffixed and unsuffixed words alike.
new_statements.first_reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.identity_note: Zorc 1977's 'Aborlan' = Aborlan Tagbanwa [tbw] (his language list p. 25 no. 26: 'Aborlan [Tagbanwa], Aborlan (area), southern Palawan'; p. 287 n. 8 names it 'Aborlan Tagbanwa'). Reid 1971 entry 41 represents the dialect of barrio Cabigaan, Aborlan, Palawan (Hussey data). Distinct from Central Tagbanwa [tgt] (Glottolog cent2091; Scebold 2003) and Calamian/Kalamian Tagbanwa [tbk] (Kalamianic), both of which are also called 'Tagbanwa' in the literature; Thiessen 1981 groups Aborlan Tagbanwa with Batak as North Palawan.

new_statements.reading: First-hand (Zorc's own Aborlan field data): Aborlan Tagbanwa has no contrastive/phonemic word accent, i.e. no lexical stress contrasts. Placement of non-contrastive stress is not stated. Corroborated by Zorc's review of Thiessen 1981 (offprint 044, p. 109): accent differences in Aborlan 'are the result of Tagalog or Bisayan superstrata and often differ from one idiolect to another', and Thiessen 1981:10 (quoted there) says that in none of the Palawan varieties are words distinguished by accent alone, with accent on one of the last two syllables in the South Palawan varieties. A fixed-position statement for Aborlan itself would need Thiessen 1980/1981 or Hussey 1963/1965, neither of which is online.

new_statements.relation_note: Same content as the existing_statements (which already cite this offprint second-hand): no contrastive word accent in Aborlan; placement not stated. Adds the verbatim Thiessen 1981:10 wording and makes explicit that the 'last two syllables' clause does not cover Aborlan (a North Palawan variety in Thiessen's grouping). The catalog record's empty rule is consistent with this.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent in Aborlan Tagbanwa is not phonemic: no words are distinguished by accent alone (Thiessen 1981:10, covering all seven Palawan varieties incl. Aborlan), and Zorc's own Aborlan data show that the accent differences that do occur are idiolectal imitations of Tagalog or Bisayan forms. Where the (non-contrastive) accent falls in Aborlan is not stated; Thiessen's 'one of the last two syllables' placement is given only for the South Palawan varieties (Quezon, Brooke's Point, Canipaan, Molbog), and Zorc says it is ambiguous between a regular oxytone/paroxytone pattern per dialect and sporadic unpredictable accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Zorc: Warren 1959 lists Batak minimal pairs (dato 'that' : dató 'chief'; dúdu? 'father's or mother's sister' : dudú? 'breast, teat') that contradict Thiessen's non-contrastiveness claim, but for Batak, not Aborlan; contrasts that occur now 'are the result of mimicry of Tagalog or Bisayan forms known to and by individual speakers'. Zorc adds that 'the accent situation on Palawan requires more detailed study'. Journal not identified: no header on the offprint, not in Zorc's 2020 CV or 2019 resume (downloaded from zorc.net), no CrossRef hit; dated 1984-86 from the affiliation (School of Australian Linguistics, Darwin Institute of Technology, so named from 1984; Zorc left SAL 08/1986 per CV) and the citation of Zorc 1983 PJL 14.1 as published.
new_statements.identity_note: Zorc's first-hand data are from Aborlan (Aborlan area, southern Palawan; Zorc 1977 p. 25 no. 26 and p. 287 n. 8). In Thiessen 1981 Aborlan Tagbanwa is grouped with Batak as North Palawan; the 'last two syllables' accent statement Zorc quotes is for the South Palawan varieties (Quezon, Brooke's Point, Canipaan, Molbog), not Aborlan. The listed SIL search code xsb is Sambal; Aborlan Tagbanwa is tbw, and the holdings listed here are the tbw-tagged ones (Calamian tbk and Central tgt items excluded).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Hussey, Stewart & Jean Hussey. 1963. The phonemes of Tagbanwa (SIL Philippine Branch; archives/93115), section 4, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 6): stress is predictable on the penultimate syllable of words within a grammatical frame; a few speakers shift stress to the ultima on utterance-final words; stress is nonphonemic. This is the fixed-position statement for Aborlan Tagbanwa that the reader and the existing_statements said was not online; it is now obtained by the project as page image checked). Nothing missed in Morphophonemics 1963 or Green & Hale 1977 (both silent on stress).

readall_conflicts: No disagreement between the opened sources about Aborlan itself: Zorc 1977 (already in the catalog) and Zorc's review of Thiessen 1981 both say Aborlan Tagbanwa has no contrastive word accent, and neither states a fixed position for the non-contrastive accent. Within the review Zorc flags two internal tensions that concern other Palawan varieties: Thiessen's placement statement ('one of the last two syllables', given only for the South Palawan varieties Quezon, Brooke's Point, Canipaan and Molbog) is ambiguous between regular final/penult accent per dialect and sporadic unpredictable accent, and Warren 1959's Batak minimal pairs contradict Thiessen's claim of non-contrastiveness for Batak. The SIL phonology sources (Hussey & Hussey 1963 'The phonemes of Tagbanwa'; Green 1977; Green 1979 word list) could not be read (could not be reached by automated download file host), so a possible fixed-position statement for Aborlan remains unchecked.
